findings: File has exactly 0 dollar signs ($) — no $ figures, no program $ claims, no price claims exist in the body.

USPS mail forwarding is mentioned at lines 34 ('Set up mail forwarding for the final bill') and 78 ('Set up forwarding at least a week before you leave'). No dollar amount or duration (months) is claimed — the file simply advises forwarding. USPS.com (retrieved 2026-08-29) states: identity verification fee $1.25; standard forwarding lasts 12 months with optional 6/12/18-month extensions; mail forwarding may begin within 3 business days, best to allow up to 2 weeks. The file's '1 week out' recommendation falls within USPS's 'best to allow up to 2 weeks' window — consistent.

Utility notice-period claim at line 39: 'many need 3–10 business days' notice for a scheduled disconnect or connect.' This is a general industry range. Attempts to fetch PG&E, Duke Energy, Con Edison, and National Grid move-service pages all returned 404 or JavaScript-gated pages within the run's fetch budget. Cannot anchor to a specific utility quote. Recommend sourcing to a general industry reference or removing.

Utility lead-time recommendation at line 19: 'Call 2+ weeks ahead' and at line 39/132: 'start at 3 weeks, not 2' for new territory. These are practical recommendations, not provider-mandated policies. Same sourcing limitation applies.

Deposit mechanics claims (lines 55-59): deposits waived with autopay/good-credit letter; paid in installments; refundable after a year of on-time payments; old deposit refunded after final bill settled. These are generally accurate across US utilities (confirmed by Known Facts: TX 1/5 annual cap, SMUD $27.00/mo as deposit anchors from other articles). Recommend keeping but adding source.
Proration claims (lines 69, 85): final bill prorated 'pay only for the days you actually used service.' Standard utility billing practice. Correct.
Energy.gov/energysaver URLs: none appear in this file — no replacement needed.
No date claims beyond the relative timeline (weeks/days). The date value 'move on the 15th' (line 85) is an example, not a hard claim.

File has H2 headings: Quick Answer, The Timeline: 4 Weeks Out → Moving Day, Turn-Off vs. Transfer, Deposits/Connection Fees, The Final Bill, What People Forget, Special Cases, Checklist, FAQ, Image Prompts — 10 H2s counted, matches mission.
